items.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: I worked with a lot of singers — Peggy Lee, Ella Fitz

ctx.x: That’s a kind of a high pressure job for a first one, too. © Fillius Jazz Archive -2-

It really was. And I was still wet behind the ears as it were, and, but Stan was good. He nurtured me and helped me along and after that band I did several other road bands — Neal Hefti’s band and Billy May, Charlie Barnet; and I worked with a lot of singers — Peggy Lee, Ella Fitz, I worked with Dorothy Dandridge for a while and then she had a sad ending, committed suicide. But I also worked with Betty Hutton. I did a lot of those kind of things. The only, and we were just mentioning about Andre Previn. I worked…
Not too many people have gone that route.

items.title: Frank Capp interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995
items.q: Frank has played behind some of the great singers, including Ella Fitzgerald

ctx.x: Born in Worcester, Massachusetts in 1931, he attended Boston University and got his first break in the music business by replacing Shelly Manne in Stan Kenton’s orchestra in 1951. His subsequent big band work included gigs with Billy May and Neal Hefti. In the late 50s he found a home at the West Coast Warner Brothers studio, recording for numerous T.V. and film scores and playing with the popular Andre Previn Trio. He became part of the vital West Coast jazz scene, performing with Marty Paich, Art Pepper and…
Frank has played behind some of the great singers, including Ella Fitzgerald, Ernestine Anderson and Joe Williams. In 1975 he founded the Capp-Pierce Juggernaut with Pianist Nat Pierce.
Frank was interviewed in Los Angeles on September 3, 1995 by Monk Rowe.
